newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eduscho hopes to get approval for sale to Tchibo.
newsitem.headline: Eduscho hopes to get approval for sale to Tchibo.

text.p: Eduscho GmbH & Co KG is optimistic monopoly authorities will approve a planned sale of the firm to competitor Tchibo Holding AG, Eduscho spokesman Rolf Helmbrecht said on Wednesday.
Helmbrecht said while the companies represented a sizeable share of the German coffee market, their combined strength in Europe as a whole would be much smaller.
The two companies sell roasted coffee and consumer goods in tied outlets.
Eduscho expects net sales of 2.25 billion marks in 1996, of which a little more than half would be derived from coffee.
It operates 620 shops in Germany and 150 in Austria but if Eduscho stalls in bakeries and groceries are added, it has more than 20,000 sales points.
Eduscho is not listed. It is owned by the Schopf family, with main shareholder Rolf Schopf.

Helmbrecht said there were no large-scale plans to dismiss members of its 5,250-strong workforce or to close shops if the purchase by Tchibo went ahead, at least not beyond previous practice of closing unprofitable locations.
